title: What this console remembers
summary: The pair to LLM data: the live journal, the vault of filed sessions, the sealed archive and the event journal - what it still has, and what was folded away.

surfaces.usb: DEGRADED(promotion pending - authored and certified on PC first, then carried to the stick per-file and hash-verified, where the stick runs its own suite)
surfaces.web: N/A(by steward decision 2026-09-20: the web portal does not need these modules - a browser tab has no journal, no vault and no record to report on, so a card there could only be decoration)

notes: Read-out (family 'info'), the pair to lygo.llminfo: llminfo reports what the brain is, this reports what the console still has and what was summarised away. Five stores, each asked of its OWNER and never re-derived: compaction.safe_status() for the live journal, the window and the sealed archive; sessions.safe_stats() for the vault; paths for the event journal's location; receipts for the rotation policy that bounds the append-only stores. It owns no state, writes nothing and gates nothing, and its test scans its own source for write calls. THE DIVISION OF FACTS: the live token budget and the model's context window belong to lygo.llminfo - this card prints a row NAMING that owner instead of a second copy of the number that could drift out of step. HONESTY: every number a store could not produce is a named gap in missing[] and drags the card off green; a store that really is empty is a true fact and stays green ('nothing sealed yet - a true fact on a fresh kit, not a gap'); the recall reach group prints the rule table it counted by (newest 8 archives, 700-char snippets, a query needs a word of 4+ letters) so 'nothing was lost' is a claim about a named search. A zip the index names but cannot find is amber with the reason: the index stores an absolute path, so a moved or copied tree can leave it pointing home.
